record.original_question: For a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold M and a volume-preserving H^s diffeomorphism phi of M, determine whether phi lies in the image of the L2 exponential map on D_mu^s(M) and whether there exists an energy-minimizing L2 geodesic from the identity to phi.

evidence.quote: Problem 8 (Two-point boundary value problem). Let M be a compact two-dimensional Rieman- nian manifold and let ϕ be a volume-preserving diffeomorphism of M of Sobolev class H s . (i) (Surjectivity Problem) Find a divergence-free vector field v ∈ H s (M ) such that expe v = ϕ. (ii) (Variational Problem) Find a curve γ(t) in Dµs (M ) from e to ϕ which minimizes the L2 R1 energy functional E(γ) = 21 0 kγ̇(t)k2L2 dt. Although two-point boundary value problems in hydrodynamics are no less fundamental than the Cauchy problem they have not received as much attention. From the geometric point of view (i) and (ii) may be regarded as infinite-dimensional versions of the classical Hopf–Rinow theorem. One strategy for (i) is to follow the classical argument of Hopf and Rinow compensating for the lack of local compactness with a priori estimates derived with the help of weak solutions and Lyapunov functions [128]. Another approach could use the properties of the exponential map as a nonlinear Fredholm and quasiruled map [37, 125, 130]. In connection with (ii) we mention a surprising result of [126, 127] that there exist volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of a simply connected compact 3-manifold which cannot be joined by a shortest path in Dµs (M ). For the two dimensional case partial results can be found in [100].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a compact two-dimensional Riemannian manifold (possibly with boundary), and let $s > 2$. Denote by $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ the group of orientation-preserving, volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of $M$ of Sobolev class $H^s$. This group carries a smooth Hilbert manifold structure, and equipping its tangent space at the identity $e$ — the space of divergence-free $H^s$ vector fields on $M$ tangent to $\partial M$ — with the $L^2$ inner product $\langle u, v\rangle_{L^2} = \int_M \langle u(x), v(x)\rangle\, d\mu(x)$ and extending by right-translation yields a smooth weak Riemannian metric on $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ whose geodesics correspond (via Arnold's theorem) to solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on $M$. Let $\exp_e : T_e \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M) \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ denote the associated Riemannian exponential map at the identity.

Let $\varphi \in \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ be arbitrary.

(i) (Surjectivity Problem.) Determine whether there exists a divergence-free $H^s$ vector field $v$ on $M$ such that $\exp_e v = \varphi$.

(ii) (Variational Problem.) Determine whether there exists a curve $\gamma : [0,1] \to \mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$ with $\gamma(0) = e$ and $\gamma(1) = \varphi$ that minimizes the energy functional
$$E(\gamma) = \tfrac{1}{2}\int_0^1 \|\dot\gamma(t)\|_{L^2}^2\, dt$$
among all such $H^1$ paths in $\mathcal{D}^s_\mu(M)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The two-point boundary value problem for the $L^2$ exponential map on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of a compact 2-manifold is a long-standing open problem. Partial results exist: in 2D the exponential map is a nonlinear Fredholm map of index zero (Ebin–Misiołek–Preston and subsequent work), and normal forms near conjugate points have been studied, but neither global surjectivity nor existence of minimizing $L^2$ geodesics between arbitrary volumorphisms has been established.

status_evidence.title: The Exponential Map of the Group of Area-Preserving Diffeomorphisms of a Surface with Boundary
status_evidence.snippet: The Riemannian exponential map of the right-invariant L² metric on the group of volume-preserving diffeomorphisms of a two-dimensional manifold with a nonempty boundary is a nonlinear Fredholm map of index zero.
status_evidence.claim: Fredholm property of the L^2 exponential map in 2D is established, a partial step toward surjectivity, but global surjectivity to arbitrary volumorphisms remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Normal Forms for the L2 Riemannian Exponential Map on Diffeomorphism Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Normal forms for the L² exponential map near conjugate points on diffeomorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Local structure near conjugate points has been described, but the global two-point boundary value problem is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: The Exponential Map Near Conjugate Points In 2D Hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Studies behavior of the exponential map near conjugate vectors in 2D volumorphism groups.
status_evidence.claim: Only local results near conjugate points are obtained; the surjectivity and minimizing-geodesic questions remain open.
